title: Parity Fixture
description: A single baseline-vs-Praxis-candidate parity comparison fixture: which legacy nodes/events a workload expects, which of those are expressible through the current overlay, and the deterministic FakeExecutor script that drives the overlay's expressible subset to a terminal status. Generic field names only -- domain-specific vocabulary lives in fixture instances (benchmark/fixtures/*.json), never in this schema.

workload_id.description: Cites an exact external workload identifier, e.g. a benchmark/corpus/*.md filename -- never a paraphrase. The schema can only check it's a non-empty string; the exact-filename convention is enforced by the fixture's own test.

node_or_event.description: A bare legacy node id or event name only, e.g. `plan_bundle` or `VERIFY_DONE` -- never prose. A caveat that doesn't fit this shape belongs in the fixture's top-level `notes` array instead, so it stays structurally visible to documentation generation rather than silently falling out of it.

notes.description: Fixture-level prose disclosures that don't fit legacy_expected's node/event shape (e.g. explaining why a praxis_script drives every overlay node to a terminal status even though the scenario's own defining behavior isn't expressible). Optional; omit if a fixture needs no such caveat.

praxis_script.description: Maps an overlay node id to its scripted outcome, exactly the shape praxis_runtime.testing.fake_executor.FakeExecutor consumes as its `script` argument: {node_id: {event_type, evidence}}, where evidence is passed straight through to TransitionEngine.apply(node_id, event_type, evidence=...).
